takeaways.label: Record quarter, structurally upgraded
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 145% YoY to INR2,529 crores, the second consecutive record quarter, driven by a structural shift from spot orders to scheduled multiyear backlog.

takeaways.label: Margin target raised on mix shift
takeaways.text: Operational EBITDA margin hit 27.1% in Q2, and the FY29 Lakshya margin target was upgraded to ~30% from 27%, reflecting confidence in the higher-margin Data Center portfolio.

takeaways.label: Order book swells to INR35,274 crores
takeaways.text: H1 order intake of INR32,000 crores was roughly 4x all of FY26, headlined by a new 5-year \$1.2 billion hyperscaler agreement for AI-ready optical solutions.

takeaways.label: Data Center pivot is working
takeaways.text: The segment contributed 33% of H1 revenue, and the company is on track to scale it to 50% in FY27, with optical connectivity attach rates reaching an all-time high of 24%.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the 27%+ margin run-rate sustains as guided, the pace of Data Center revenue scaling toward 50%, and progress on the INR3,021 crores of order book scheduled for Q3 execution.

points.label: Fiber is the backbone
points.text: Management’s core thesis is that AI-era infrastructure runs on optical fiber, with global data center capacity expected to grow from ~82 GW to ~219 GW by 2030, over 70% from AI-specific infrastructure.

points.label: Fiber intensity multiplying
points.text: Upcoming architectures are heading toward 16,000 fibers per switch rack, while scale-across dynamics multiply interconnects and 1.6 terabit speeds make optical fiber non-negotiable.

points.label: Demand visibility extends well beyond 2030
points.text: Hyperscaler power-side contracts already stretch into 2031 and 2032, giving management comfort that investments by the larger hyperscalers will continue well beyond 2030.

points.label: India data center buildout
points.text: Installed capacity is set to increase nearly sixfold to ~10.5 GW by 2031, adding a domestic demand layer to the global hyperscaler story.

points.label: Global fiber demand forecast
points.text: CRU expects global optical cable demand to reach 85.1 crore fiber km by 2031 at a 7.5% CAGR, with AI data centers capturing one-third of total volume share outside China by 2030, and STL’s focused markets leading with a 15.7% CAGR in 2030.

quotes.text: Ankit Agarwal: "The world is building infrastructure for the AI era and the infrastructure runs on optical fiber."

points.label: Order book at record INR35,274 crores
points.text: Up 4.6x from INR7,687 crores at the start of FY27, reflecting strong order inflows and long-term customer commitments.

points.label: H1 order intake of INR32,000 crores
points.text: Roughly 4x the orders won in all of FY26, with the largest win being a new 5-year \$1.2 billion agreement with a global hyperscaler for AI-ready optical solutions, building on a \$1.11 billion award letter from another hyperscaler last quarter.

points.label: Structural shift in revenue composition
points.text: Historically, a meaningful share of quarterly revenue came from spot orders won and delivered within the same quarter; now, as multiyear agreements scale, more revenue comes from scheduled backlog, giving more predictable revenue, better capacity planning, and more stable realization.

points.label: Near-term execution visibility
points.text: ~INR3,021 crores of the open order book is scheduled for execution in Q3 FY27, with the rest over Q4 FY27 and beyond.

points.label: Pipeline remains active
points.text: The company continues conversations with other data center companies and telecom operators, looking to maximize further partnerships as capacities come up in the coming 2 to 3 years.

quotes.text: Ajay Jhanjhari: "Historically, a meaningful share of each quarter's revenue came from spot orders won and delivered within the same quarter. As our multiyear agreements with hyperscalers and telecom operators scale up, more of our revenue now comes from the scheduled backlog and spot business makes up a negligible share."

points.label: Data Center contributed 33% of H1 FY27 revenue
points.text: The company is on track to scale this segment to 50% of revenues in the current fiscal year, with management confident the share will land in the 50% to 60% range by design, balancing geography and customer mix.

points.label: Optical connectivity attach rate at all-time high of 24%
points.text: Up from 20% in H1 FY26 and achieved on a much larger OFC revenue base, demonstrating the strategic pivot toward higher value-added integrated solutions; the company remains focused on driving this to 25% and beyond in FY27.

points.label: Neuralis portfolio expansion
points.text: Launched Pre-Terminated Trunk Assemblies in September, factory-built plug-and-play installations that are 100% factory-tested and supported by local manufacturing in South Carolina, plus a new plenum-rated portfolio for inside data hall connectivity.

points.label: Next-generation fiber in motion
points.text: Hollow-Core Fiber transitioned into its first commercial pilot phase; G.654.E fiber is now fully commercialized; Multi-Core fiber has successful real-world deployments underway in India and the U.K. alongside partners like C-DOT, IIT Madras and Colt.

points.label: Global market share rising
points.text: Global ex-China OFC market share increased to 9% in H1 FY27 from 7% in H1 FY26.

points.label: Product mix shifting up
points.text: More and more of sales will be high-end products under the Neuralis portfolio and high-end connectivity products like CONCAT and MMC connectivity, supporting the margin upgrade story.

quotes.text: Ankit Agarwal: "I think broadly, we’ve guided that we feel confident that our DC share will be close to around 50%, and then I think by design, that’s something that we’re driving that it should be in this 50% to 60% share because we also want to have a good mix of customers both from a geography perspective as well as customer base."

points.label: Operational EBITDA margin of 27.1% in Q2
points.text: Expanded 624 bps QoQ, driven by higher capacity utilization, richer product and customer mix, and increasing share of high-value optical connectivity; reported EBITDA of INR846 crores included a one-time net gain of INR161 crores from a U.S. tariff refund.

points.label: FY29 Lakshya margin target upgraded to ~30%
points.text: Raised from 27% earlier, driven by strong mix shift toward the higher-margin Data Center portfolio, improved attach rate, and confidence from the INR35,000 crores order book.

points.label: H1 FY27 margin was 23%
points.text: Management corrected an analyst’s 24% figure, and plans to perform at or better than the Q2 reported level of 27% going forward, aligning results with the increased 30% Lakshya target.

points.label: Record PAT of INR517 crores in Q2
points.text: H1 PAT reached INR714 crores versus INR14 crores in H1 FY26, reflecting strong operating leverage as revenue scales.

points.label: Finance costs to reduce from Q3
points.text: Finance costs rose 15% YoY in Q2 because the company prepaid some loans that were due later, incurring prepayment penalties; net finance costs are expected to reduce from Q3 onwards.

points.label: One-time items cleared
points.text: INR49 crores impairment plus INR22 crores additional depreciation related to subsidiary Speedon Networks was taken to square it off in full; a INR161 crores U.S. tariff refund was received with a small Phase 3 amount already applied for and pending.

quotes.text: Ajay Jhanjhari: "The strong margin expansion we are delivering today, combined with the multiyear visibility from our record order book gives us stronger confidence to raise the bar on our profitability."

points.label: Net cash balance improved to INR703 crores
points.text: Up from INR483 crores last quarter, and the company continues to be net debt-free.

points.label: Credit rating upgraded
points.text: CRISIL upgraded the long-term rating to AA stable from AA-, and both CRISIL and ICRA now rate STL at AA stable, reflecting the strengthened financial profile.

points.label: Capex plan of INR1,000 crores per year from 2027 to 2029
points.text: For brownfield expansion of preform, fiber and cable capacity by 50%, plus a greenfield facility for pre-term solutions to increase termination capability.

points.label: Utilization improving quarter-on-quarter
points.text: Improvement driven by better ability to procure raw materials like germanium and helium, plus diversification in key raw materials; capacity projects to start coming online in the next few quarters.

points.label: Net working capital expected stable in 45 to 50 day range
points.text: Payable days fell sharply because payment terms for materials changed in a supply-constrained market, but are expected to remain stable going forward; improvements in debtors and inventory to reflect from next quarter.

points.label: Sustainability milestone
points.text: The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant transitioned to 100% green power, slashing fiber carbon footprint by over 80% while maintaining zero waste to landfill and zero liquid discharge; the company remains committed to achieving net zero by 2030.

points.label: R&D commitment at 2% of annual revenue
points.text: Directed into next-generation optical platforms including Hollow-Core Fiber, Multi-Core Fiber, and G.654.E fiber, all of which are now in commercial pilot or fully commercialized stages.

points.label: Patent portfolio growing
points.text: 49 new filings this quarter brought the total portfolio to over 805 patents, and STL was recognized on IAM’s Asia IP Elite 2026 list.

points.label: Hollow-Core and Multi-Core fiber progressing
points.text: Scale is expected to start improving in another 1.5 to 2 years, with active work underway on production capabilities and with installers and customers for deployment; trials conducted in India for Hollow-Core and in the U.K. for Multi-Core.

points.label: Attach rate journey is about innovation, not just capacity
points.text: Management noted that global peers have been established for a very long time with well-familiar installers, so STL’s work involves innovation and co-development with customers, building customized solutions for future requirements rather than just adding capacity.

quotes.text: Ankit Agarwal: "I think some of our global peers have been in this industry for a very, very long time. They are well-established, manufacturing, they’re well-established technology, IP and even the installers and others are really well familiar with their portfolio. So this is a work that we are doing. It’s not just about capacity. A lot of it is innovation and co-development with the customer, building things that are customized for their future requirements, not necessarily for today."

items.title: Lakshya FY29 group targets
items.text: Management's September 2026 roadmap targets ₹20,000 crore revenue in FY29 (~4x FY26's ₹4,745 crore) with EBITDA margin upgraded to ~30% from 27%, and says the order book gives stronger visibility on these targets than at announcement. H1 FY27 already delivered ₹4,439 crore revenue (+116%) at 24.4% EBITDA margin, tracking the trajectory.

items.title: Hyperscaler long-term supply agreements
items.text: Signed LTSAs include ~USD 1.2 billion (1 Oct 2026, CY26-30), ~USD 1.11 billion PAL (May 2026, FY27-29) and ~USD 288 million (Aug 2026, CY27-29), plus a ~USD 210 million telecom LTSA and ~₹960 crore domestic operator deal. H1 FY27 order intake of ₹32,000 crore - roughly 4x all of FY26 - lifted the open order book to a record ₹35,274 crore, 4.6x the start of FY27.

items.title: Data center mix shift to 50% of revenue
items.text: Data center revenue grew from 1% of FY26 sales to 33% in H1 FY27, with management guiding to ~50% this fiscal and designing for 50-60% long term. DC sales carry better margins, underpinning the guided 27%+ EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 onward.

items.title: ₹3,000 crore capacity expansion
items.text: Board approved (3 Sep 2026) ~₹3,000 crore to add ~50% to preform, fiber and cable capacity by end FY29 at ~70% current utilization, funded from internal accruals and/or debt, plus a greenfield pre-terminated solutions facility. Capacity projects start coming online over the next few quarters, removing the main constraint on converting the record order book.

items.title: Neuralis attach-rate scale-up
items.text: Attach rate hit an all-time high 24% in H1 FY27 (from 20% a year earlier) with a 25%+ target this fiscal, as Neuralis pre-terminated trunks scaling to 6,912 fibers won OFNP and US Conec certifications for hyperscale deployments. Higher attach means more high-margin connectivity sold per cable order, directly lifting blended margins.

items.title: US onshore manufacturing
items.text: A $100 million five-year investment announced May 2026 expands US connectivity capacity, complementing the fully ready Lugoff, South Carolina plant that supports Neuralis and Celesta IBR for US hyperscalers. With US tariffs cut from 50% to 15% and North America at 61% of H1 revenue, local production shortens turnaround and protects margin on the largest geography.

items.title: Next-generation fiber platforms
items.text: India's first hollow-core cable (launched March 2026, ~46% faster signal travel) entered commercial pilot in Q2 FY27, G.654.E secured its first commercial order with better realizations than standard fiber, and Multiverse multi-core fiber is in live trials with Colt, C-DOT and IIT Madras. Management expects these technologies to scale over the next 1.5-2 years, positioning STL for premium-priced AI-era demand.

items.title: CONCAT spliceless FTTH solution
items.text: Launched in the US (17 Jul 2026) after field trials on one of America's largest telecom networks, cutting installation labor cost by up to 71%. Scaling CONCAT drives higher connectivity attach rates on fiber cable sales in both US and European broadband builds.

items.title: India and US government broadband programs
items.text: BharatNet Phase 3 (₹1.39 trillion, fibre to 1.5 crore rural homes) is rolling out with Invenia's J&K package won and MAFs secured from other bidders, while the ~$97 billion US broadband funding cycle is expected to generate meaningful demand from H2 2026. Government programs could lock in ₹1,100-1,500 crore of annual India revenue.

items.title: Deleveraged balance sheet funding growth
items.text: The ₹1,500 crore QIP (2.5x subscribed, Motilal Oswal, Nomura, HSBC among investors) plus record profits took the company net cash positive at ₹703 crore in Q2 FY27, with CRISIL and ICRA both upgrading to AA/Stable. A net debt-free balance sheet lets the ₹1,000 crore annual capex plan through FY29 proceed without straining cash flow.
